title: Red Sox run out of magic, fall to the Orioles as win streak stops at 15
content:
BOSTON — The Boston Red Sox did something on Wednesday that they haven’t done in three weeks: Lose.

After the Baltimore Orioles pounced on Red Sox rookie starter Eduardo Rivera for four runs in the first inning, Boston couldn’t muster one of its magical comebacks that has been customary in recent weeks.

The Red Sox fell to the Orioles, 5-1, in the second game of a Wednesday doubleheader, snapping their win streak at 15 and costing them a chance to set a franchise record of 16 straight.

Earlier in the day, a 6-3 win over Baltimore helped the Red Sox tie the longest win streak in club history, set in 1946 by a Ted Williams-led team that went to the World Series. Now, this 2026 team will sit alongside that group in the history books.

In the midst of their improbable streak, the Red Sox had swept three straight road series before the All-Star break, besting the Los Angeles Angels, Chicago White Sox and New York Mets. They returned to action with a four-game sweep of the American League East-leading Tampa Bay Rays, and had taken the first two games against Baltimore. They had not lost a game since July 1.

Rivera, the rookie pitcher, started in place of veteran Ranger Suarez, who was set to return Wednesday from a stint on the injured list. But Suarez, who had been dealing with a groin strain, fell ill earlier in the week. That illness — coupled with a few intense workouts as he tried to prepare for a return — set him back. The Red Sox turned to Rivera, who pitched well before the break, but struggled in his most recent outing Friday. It was more of the same Wednesday. Rivera recorded just two outs and was booed as he headed back to the dugout. The Red Sox then turned to beleaguered right-hander Brayan Bello in long relief.

Bello, who had been a rotation mainstay but was demoted to Triple A earlier this season after a rough start, had been called up as a long reliever before the break. He hadn’t pitched since July 12, but tossed 5 1/3 scoreless innings on Wednesday to keep the Red Sox in the game.

The Red Sox had shown a remarkable ability for comebacks during this stretch. Six of their 15 wins were of the come-from-behind variety. They’d rallied from a deficit in four of their previous five games.

It wasn’t the case Wednesday, though. In the fourth, Willson Contreras hit a ground-rule double and scored on Masataka Yoshida’s RBI single, but that’s all the Red Sox could muster. Boston’s resilient bats had little to show against Kyle Bradish, who tossed six innings and allowed one run.

Still, this 15-game win streak, the longest in the majors since the St. Louis Cardinals’ 17-game streak in 2021, may have saved Boston’s season.

On June 24, the Red Sox owned the worst record in the American League at 32-46, 14 games under .500. Since then, they’ve reeled off wins in 20 of 23 games and now sit squarely in third place for the AL wild-card race.

What they do from here will be key. With 11 days before the Aug. 3 trade deadline, Boston has proven it is a team worthy of adding to. The Red Sox are off Thursday before three games this weekend against the struggling Toronto Blue Jays, against whom they’ll try to restart another stretch of wins.
